title: Strict-local exchange on derived global cohomology
statement: Let $A\to B$ be a local homomorphism of strictly henselian local rings [def-weil-pbc-henselian-terminology]. Let $f:X\to\operatorname{Spec}A$, $f':X'\to\operatorname{Spec}B$, and $g':X'\to X$ form a cartesian square with $g:\operatorname{Spec}B\to\operatorname{Spec}A$ [def-weil-pbc-cartesian-square]. Let $K$ be any bounded below derived object of abelian etale sheaves on $X$ [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories], and $q\in\mathbb Z$. Let $t$ be the geometric closed B-point with residue field $\kappa(B)$ [def-weil-pbc-geometric-stalks], and put $S=H^q(g^{-1}Rf_*K)$ and $T=H^q(Rf'_*g'^{-1}K)$, using [def-weil-pbc-derived-inverse-image] and [def-weil-pbc-direct-image]. Let $e:S\to T$ be homology of the derived exchange [def-weil-pbc-derived-exchange]. Write $P=R\Gamma(X,-)$ and $P'=R\Gamma(X',-)$ [def-weil-pbc-etale-cohomology], $U=H^q(PK)$ and $V=H^q(P'(g'^{-1}K))$. Let $p:U\to V$ be $H^q$ of $P$ applied to the derived adjunction unit $K\to Rg'_*g'^{-1}K$ [prop-weil-pbc-derived-inverse-image-adjunction], followed by the Leray identification [lem-weil-pbc-cohomology-pullback-derived-unit]. There exist additive equivalences $c_1:S_t\xrightarrow{\sim}U$ and $c_2:T_t\xrightarrow{\sim}V$ such that $c_2(e_t(x))=p(c_1(x))$ for every $x\in S_t$. No properness, quasi-compactness, torsion, or concentration in degree zero is assumed.

proof.text: Choose a bounded below injective representative I of K and a bounded below injective replacement J of its exact inverse image. Direct images preserve K-injectives because their left adjoints are exact. Thus the derived images are computed by f_*I and f prime_*J.

Strict-local global germs identify sections with the closed-point stalk, naturally. Locality gives a closed A-image for the B-point. Apply inverse-image stalk comparison, using the germ construction for separably closed points (or extending to algebraic closures, which are purely inseparable over them). Apply exact stalks to both complexes and commute them with homology. Leray identifies their section complexes with the complexes of global sections on X and X prime; their homologies give c1 and c2.

The termwise exchange formula computes the map as underived exchange on I followed by f prime_* of the replacement to J. The germ compatibility identifies this map with pullback of sections followed by replacement. The derived-unit description identifies that map with p; taking homology yields the commuting equation.

All replacement comparisons are unique in the homotopy category into K-injectives. Consequently they induce the comparison isomorphisms used by the actual derived functors, and the equality survives these comparisons.
